column3: The Hebrew uses singular collective “horse” and “chariot” and calls the opposing force “a people”; BSB has plural “horses, chariots” and “an army.”
The Hebrew calls those addressed “the people”; BSB calls them “the army.”
The Hebrew says “let not your heart become soft”; BSB says “Do not be fainthearted.”
The Hebrew says “to save you”; BSB says “to give you the victory.”
The Hebrew says “the people” and separately tells the man to go and return; BSB says “the army” and simply “return home.”
The Hebrew does not explicitly name “fruit,” which BSB supplies twice in describing use of the vineyard.
The Hebrew twice says to “take her”; BSB uses “married her” and “marry her.”
The Hebrew names “the people” and actively says the fearful man must not melt his brothers’ heart; BSB has “the army” and says their hearts must not melt.
The Hebrew names “the people” twice and puts commanders “at the head of the people”; BSB says “the army” and “to lead it.”
The Hebrew says to call to the city for peace; BSB says to “make an offer of peace.”
The Hebrew makes the city a singular subject that answers and opens, without explicitly naming gates; BSB uses plural “they” and supplies “their gates.”
The Hebrew continues to refer to the city as a singular subject; BSB uses plural “they.”
The Hebrew says “by the mouth of the sword”; BSB says “put ... to the sword.”
The Hebrew says to “eat” the spoil; BSB says to “use” it.
The Hebrew calls these “the cities of these nations”; BSB says the cities “belong to the nations nearby,” supplying “nearby.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew names each people with a singular collective noun; BSB uses plural names.
The Hebrew directly says “and you will sin”; BSB makes this part of what the nations cause you to do.
The Hebrew uses singular collective “tree” and says to eat “from it” without an explicit noun “fruit”; BSB uses plural “trees” and supplies “their fruit.”
The Hebrew uses singular “a tree” and separately says to destroy and cut it down; BSB uses plural “trees” and a single command to destroy them.
